 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Milwaukee Bucks will try to snap a five-game losing streak tonight, Nov. 8, when they host the Boston Celtics at Fiserv Forum. Milwaukee rallied from a 22-point first half deficit to push Boston late in a loss at TD Garden on Nov. 4. 
 Bucks working to keep vibes positive
 Through their losses, Bucks players have maintained a diplomatic approach to ending games without the result they wanted. They see improvement in small areas on a near-regular basis and believe they're knocking on the door of not just one victory, but several.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "There's a lot of basketball still left in the season," Bucks guard AJ Green said. "And it's just the start. We've made strides. It's just a matter of doing it for 48 minutes and being consistent with it. I think our spirit is still great. Our joy, our togetherness is still there. Hopefully, regardless of what happens, it's only going to come together even more whether it's through adversity or good times. I hope all of it brings us together."
 Head coach Taylor Jenkins shouldered the loss to Houston on Oct. 28, believing he didn't prepare the team well enough. Players have also taken accountability, from Jaime Jaquez Jr. admitting his late-game turnovers have hurt the team to Myles Turner acknowledging to a scoreless night is not helpful to Brayden Burries believing he rebounded better, perhaps a result could change.
 Milwaukee Bucks head coach Taylor Jenkins talks with guard Ryan Rollins (13) during the second half of their game Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 at Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The Cleveland Cavaliers beat the Milwaukee Bucks 136-111. As the team tries to keep themselves together through a rough start to the season, Jenkins is also keeping a keen eye on how they're doing so.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Obviously we're trying to set a course here, a vision, a culture, an identity and what we're trying to accomplish basketball wise and what I'm trying to do to get these guys their roles to impact winning," Jenkins said. "So, I've got to constantly be available for them.
 "So, the vibes of the team for sure I'm always going to be aware of that regardless of what the results are early in the season, late in the season, I think that's key for any head coach. You always want to be tapped into that."
 It's not the first time the Bucks' head coach has had to navigate such a beginning. His first two youthful Memphis Grizzlies teams in 2019-20 and 2020-21 began 2-7 and 2-6, respectively. The 2019-20 team dropped to 6-16 before finishing 34-39 in a COVID-19 shortened campaign.
 "Taylor's character, Taylor's attention to detail, care for the people, care for the organization, for the community, he's unbelievable," said Toronto head coach Darko Rajaković, who was an assistant under Jenkins in the 2020-21 season. "He's an amazing leader. And he sets the standard for everybody else around him. So, I'm sure that from [Nov. 7] the team is going to do much better."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bucks threatening worst start in franchise history
 The Bucks are just the third team in franchise history to start a season with one win their first nine games (1974-75 and 1993-94). In the 1974-75 season Kareem Abdul-Jabbar was out injured for the first 16 games, and this is the first season after trading Giannis Antetokounmpo. 
 The 1974-75 team had the organization's worst opening stretch, beginning 1-11 before ending November at 6-14.
 The 1993-94 team went 1-10 to start the season and ended November with a 2-12 record.
 The worst overall season in franchise history was the tanking 2013-14 campaign in which the Bucks won 15 games. That Bucks team, which featured a rookie Antetokounmpo, started 2-2 before finishing November with a 3-13 mark.
 Milwaukee Bucks starters Nov. 8
 Guards: Brayden Burries, Tyler Herro
 Forwards: Kyle Kuzma, Jaime Jaquez Jr.
 Center: Myles Turner
 Bucks injury report
 Gary Trent Jr., out (illness): Bucks head coach Taylor Jenkins said Trent is away from the team due to the illness.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement What time is the Bucks game?
 Tip-off is scheduled for 7 p.m. CT.
 What channel is the Bucks game on?
 The game will be broadcast on MY24 with Lisa Byington, Marques Johnson and Melanie Ricks on the call.
